audit_findings.title: TRA liability omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $393.2 million, equal to $2.45 per diluted share, 32.4% of bridge cash and 3.7%-4.9% of scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: The contractual TRA claim must be deducted in the equity bridge unless projected OE already bears an equivalent present-value charge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of March 31, 2026 and 2025, a liability of $ 393.2 million and $ 419.4 million , respectively, was recorded for the expected amount to be paid to the affiliate of the former parent, TPG and the TPG affiliates, of which $ 372.7 million and $ 394.9 million, respectively, were included in TRA liabilities and $ 20.5 million and $ 24.5 million , respectively, were included in other current liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge omission, not merely a possible risk. Deducting the filed liability would reduce bear, base and bull values to approximately $47.43, $55.09 and $64.07 per share. It would not reverse the present no-buy conclusion at $84.50, but the adjustment is large enough to affect valuation thresholds and margin-of-safety decisions.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario with the full $393.2 million TRA liability deducted, or document and reconcile an equivalent charge already included in projected OE.

audit_findings.title: Terminal value capitalizes a temporary 45X subsidy
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 cost of sales was reduced by $379.9 million; this is 66.6% of the $570.0 million OE anchor by scale, while the after-tax OE effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The subsidy raises current operating earnings and the OE anchor, which is then grown and included in terminal value even though the credit phases down during 2030-2032 and ends thereafter.
audit_findings.evidence: The Section 45X Credit amount will be reduced each year by 25% starting in 2030 and end after 2032.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary benefit and statutory phaseout are demonstrated, while replacement by pricing, productivity or other economics is not established. With roughly half of operating value coming from terminal value, perpetuating an unnormalized anchor is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate the after-tax OE contribution from vendor rebates and assigned credits, model the statutory phaseout through 2032, test FEOC eligibility and supplier-sharing terms, and rerun all scenarios using post-credit steady-state OE.

audit_findings.title: Every scenario may miss the disclosed post-incentive volume contraction
audit_findings.magnitude: U.S. revenue was $2,730.7 million, or 77% of FY2026 revenue, and $775.6 million, or 83% of first-quarter FY2027 revenue; the resulting OE reduction is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A post-incentive reduction in U.S. project volume could lower normalized revenue, margins and OE below the FY2026 anchor and require negative near-term growth, which no scenario presently models.
audit_findings.evidence: Such acceleration in the expiration of these tax credits will reduce the number of projects in future years that would have otherwise qualified for such credits, likely reducing the overall project volume over time.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing expressly anticipates fewer qualifying projects and likely lower volume. The size and timing of the net decline remain unresolved, but the U.S. concentration and absence of any contraction scenario make the issue reasonably capable of materially changing normalized OE and the valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Rerun a post-2027 contraction case using project-level backlog timing, replacement-demand evidence, U.S. margin sensitivity and separately supported offsets from international and non-tracker businesses.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Acquisition cash payments were $144.7 million in FY2025 and $117.2 million in FY2026, with $12.2 million contributed to the joint venture; acquisitions completed after July 3, 2026 required another $196.0 million of closing cash, $50.0 million of stock consideration and up to $199.5 million of contingent cash consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: If forecast platform or solution-mix growth depends on acquisitions, excluding acquisition and strategic-investment costs from OE treats purchased growth as internally generated distributable cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in investing activities was approximately $186.9 million and directly attributable to the $117.2 million payment for all business acquisitions completed in fiscal year 2026 net of cash acquired, coupled with $49.3 million paid for the purchase of property and equipment, and $12.2 million of cash contributed to the Nextpower Arabia joint venture.
audit_findings.explanation: Repeated acquisition spending is demonstrated, but the record does not separate organic growth embedded in the scenarios from acquired growth or identify the recurring acquisition requirement. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the current model, especially because the valuation perimeter is unspecified.
audit_findings.action: Define the valuation perimeter, reconcile forecast growth to organic and acquired contributors, incorporate post-quarter acquisitions, and rerun with either fully organic assumptions or a supported recurring acquisition and strategic-investment charge.

audit_findings.title: FY2026 contains an unusual bill-and-hold revenue contribution
audit_findings.magnitude: $144.4 million of revenue, equal to 4.1% of FY2026 revenue; attributable gross profit and OE are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any revenue or profit pulled forward into FY2026 inflates the OE anchor and may create a corresponding revenue and cash-flow shortfall in later forecast periods.
audit_findings.evidence: During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, the Company recognized $ 144.4 million from certain customers under a bill-and-hold arrangement.
audit_findings.explanation: The unusual revenue contribution and absence of bill-and-hold revenue in the prior two years are demonstrated. The record does not disclose its margin, cash collection, remaining costs or whether it represents timing rather than incremental demand, so the effect on the $570.0 million anchor cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain contract-level gross profit, tax, working-capital collection and remaining-performance-cost data, identify displaced future-period sales, and rerun the valuation with any timing-related OE removed from the anchor and restored to the proper period.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earnouts are another omitted claim on cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.9 million recorded at July 3, 2026, equal to $0.22 per diluted share and 0.38% of base equity value; subsequently completed acquisitions added up to $199.5 million of maximum contingent cash consideration, whose expected fair value is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Earnouts attributable to businesses inside the earnings perimeter are debt-like claims on corporate cash and belong in the equity bridge unless their settlement cost is charged through projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Other liabilities primarily consist of long-term lease liabilities, as disclosed in the "Leases" section below, contingent earnouts for the Company’s acquisitions of $ 38.6 million and $ 2.6 million, and the long-term portion of standard product warranty liabilities of $ 8.0 million and $ 6.4 million as of March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The existing $34.9 million liability is a demonstrated omission but is not independently large enough to change the valuation conclusion. The post-quarter earnouts increase the possible exposure to about $234.4 million, or $1.46 per diluted share and 2.5% of base equity value, but maximum payouts are not expected values and their acquisition-date fair values are unavailable; broader materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Determine acquisition-date and valuation-date fair values, maximum payouts and deferred consideration for every completed acquisition, confirm which acquired earnings enter the forecast, and rerun the bridge deducting all corresponding claims not charged through OE.
